Clamp with min and max when a budget or limit exists, and say so in the description. Store the emitted number, not the formatted display string. Don't use it for values without a currency; use NumberInput. Don't use one field for multi-currency entry; pair a currency Select with the amount. The user enters a monetary amount in a known currency, such as prices, budgets, or invoice totals. The value is a plain number without a currency; use NumberInput instead. For multi-currency entry, pair a Select with NumberInput. Emits the parsed number on every edit (undefined when emptied) and formats the display with Intl.NumberFormat on blur, clamping to min/max. The field stretches to fill its container; the leading symbol addon stays a fixed width. The visible label is associated with the input; use aria-label when there is no visible label. Clamped budget min and max clamp the committed amount on blur, and a description explains the limits.

Calendar popover The month grid with full keyboard navigation. Month navigation Previous and next buttons around an announced month label. Day cells Grid buttons bounded by the min and max dates. Set minDate and maxDate when only a planning window is valid. Explain what the date drives, like a milestone, in the description. Keep the caller-owned value as a Date, not a string. Don't stack two pickers for a range; set selection="range". Don't expect free-typed input; the calendar is the parser. Don't disable dates silently; state the valid window in the description. Users pick a calendar date, month, year, timestamp, or date range. The value is free-form text; use Input. mode switches the popover between day, month, year, and datetime panels; selection="range" turns two clicks into {from, to} with presets and a connected band. The popover collision-handles; the field keeps its layout width. Day, month, and year buttons use a roving tab index, so each panel is a single Tab stop. The month label, visible year, and decade range are announced with aria-live as the view changes. Dates outside minDate and maxDate are disabled and cannot be selected. Range start and end days expose their state through aria-pressed, and today keeps aria-current date. In datetime mode the time fields reuse the TimePicker group with labeled Hour and Minutes inputs, and Done closes the popover. Arrow Down Opens the popover from the field. Arrow Left Arrow Right Moves the focused day by one day; in month or year mode, moves by one month or year. In RTL layouts the horizontal directions flip with the grid. Arrow Up Arrow Down Moves the focused day by one week; in month or year mode, moves by one row. Home End Jumps to the first or last month of the year, or year of the decade page. Enter Space Selects the focused day, month, or year; in range mode, picks the start then the end. Calendar selection Arrows move between days, Enter selects, min and max bound the range. Bounded planning window minDate and maxDate limit picking to the current sprint window. Month mode mode="month" shows twelve months with a year stepper and commits the first of the chosen month. Year mode mode="year" pages years by decade and commits January 1 of the chosen year. Date and time mode="datetime" pairs the day grid with time fields; the popover stays open until Done. Range selection selection="range" turns two clicks into {from, to}, with presets and a connected band between the endpoints.
description-list: A label/value definition list for detail pages, stacked or two-column. Term (dt) The muted label on the left of each row. dialog: A modal surface that owns focus management, naming, dismissal, and scroll locking; placement renders it centered, fullscreen, as a left/right drawer, or as a bottom sheet. Use a verb-led title that states the outcome, like "Archive project?". Keep the content short; move long forms into a dedicated page or placement="fullscreen". Restore focus to the trigger when the dialog closes (built in). Don't stack a second dialog on top of an open one. Don't use a dialog for destructive confirmations; use AlertDialog. Focus is trapped, Escape dismisses, and focus returns to the trigger, for every placement. placement="bottom" snaps to half or full viewport height; the left and right placements size with the width prop, and placement="fullscreen" always fills the viewport. Background content is scroll-locked while the dialog is open. Every placement (center, fullscreen, left, right, bottom) shares the same focus model and naming. When neither title nor description is given, a visually hidden "Dialog" title keeps the surface named. The drag handle on the bottom placement is a visual affordance only and is hidden from assistive technology. Escape Closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger. Tab Shift+Tab Cycles focus through the focusable elements inside the dialog. Confirmation Dialog traps focus, restores it on close, and dismisses with Escape or the scrim. Form dialog size="lg" gives a short form room; Field wraps each Input with a label and description. Destructive confirmation Use a danger action only when the consequence is clear and reversible where possible. Long-form task For focused tasks, keep the title visible and let the dialog body own its scroll. Fullscreen task placement="fullscreen" fills the viewport with a sticky header, scrollable body, and footer actions. Drawer panel placement="right" (or "left") slides a panel in from the edge; width sets its size. Bottom sheet placement="bottom" rises from the thumb zone; snap="half" keeps page context visible. Full-height sheet snap="full" gives long content like pickers the full viewport height.

Users must edit or comment on individual lines; use a full code review surface instead. Given oldValue/newValue it computes a line-level LCS diff; given hunks it renders them verbatim. Added lines are tinted primary, removed lines error, and screen readers hear an Added/Removed/Unchanged prefix per line. Scrolls horizontally within its bordered pane so long lines never break the layout. Each line carries a visually hidden Added, Removed, or Unchanged prefix so the change type is not conveyed by color alone. The gutter signs and line numbers are aria-hidden to keep the screen-reader output linear. From two strings Computes the line diff itself from oldValue and newValue, including dual line-number gutters. Pre-computed hunks Accepts explicit add/remove/context lines, useful when the diff comes from git or a server.
dock: A macOS-style dock of icon buttons with hover tooltips, accessible names, and an active-app indicator dot. Dock Centered icon bar rendered as a named navigation landmark. Every item is a real button whose label prop is both the accessible name and the tooltip text; active adds a non-interactive indicator dot. The dock sizes to its icons and centers in available space; on narrow screens keep the item count low or allow horizontal scrolling in a wrapper. Renders a navigation landmark labelled "Dock" by default. Each item's label becomes its aria-label, so icon-only buttons stay announced. App dock Icon buttons lift on hover and show a tooltip label; active apps get a dot underneath. Custom landmark name A custom aria-label scopes the dock when several navigation landmarks share the page.
ecosystem-rail: A persistent cross-product rail with a stable Home destination, caller-filtered applications, and honest health status. editable: Click-to-edit text that commits on Enter or blur and cancels with Escape. Preview The button that shows the current value and starts editing on activation. Don't hide the edit affordance; the pencil communicates interactivity. A displayed value is renamed or corrected in place. The value is edited alongside others in a form; use Field and Input. Enter and blur commit, Escape cancels, and the draft is preselected. The preview truncates within its container width. The preview is a real button showing the value or placeholder, so the entry point is keyboard reachable. The edit input autofocuses with the current value preselected and is named by the label. empty-state: An explanatory empty result with an optional action and SVG icon. Icon well Rounded container holding a decorative SVG icon; hidden from assistive technology. Title Heading naming the empty condition; renders h3 by default and adjusts with titleAs. Description Short explanation of why the surface is empty and what happens next. Action Caller-supplied next step, usually a single primary Button. Lead with what happened, then offer one clear next action. Distinguish a first-run empty surface from a filtered no-results state in the copy. Don't use an empty state while content is still loading; use Skeleton or LoadingState. Don't stack several competing actions under one empty state. A product surface has no results or has not been configured. Content is merely loading or filtered temporarily. Explain what happened and give one clear next action when useful. Keep the message readable and center the action beneath it. The title renders as an h3 by default; adjust titleAs so the empty state fits the page outline. The action is a real button or link; keep to a single primary action. The status icon is always aria-hidden, including custom icon overrides; the title and description carry the meaning. First-run Pair a short explanation with a single primary action. Filtered empty result Explain that filters produced no results and offer a way to adjust them. error-boundary: A class-based error boundary that isolates render failures behind a fallback UI with reset support. Boundary Class component that catches render errors from its subtree and reports them through onError. Fallback Node or render prop receiving (error, reset) that is shown while the subtree is failed. Give the fallback a recovery path through the reset callback. Don't catch expected async errors here; handle those in data-loading code with EmptyState or Alert. Don't wrap the entire app in one boundary; a single failure then blanks the whole page. A subtree can fail independently — dashboards, widgets, or third-party embeds — and the rest of the page must survive. Handling expected async errors; catch those in data-loading code and show EmptyState or Alert instead. Catches render errors below it, calls onError, swaps in the fallback, and re-renders children on reset() or when any resetKey changes. Layout-agnostic; the fallback owns its own sizing. Give the fallback an accessible error message, for example role="alert", so the failure is announced. Provide a keyboard-reachable recovery action such as a retry button. Recoverable fallback A render-prop fallback that shows the error and offers a retry via the reset callback. Static fallback A plain React node shown whenever the protected subtree throws.
expandable-card: A card that expands and collapses its extra content with a built-in trigger, chevron affordance, and smooth height animation. Header The always-visible title area, rendered as a configurable heading (h2 by default). Trigger The button with aria-expanded and the rotating chevron affordance. Region The collapsible content area, aria-hidden and inert while collapsed. Use it for secondary detail most readers skip, like changelogs or advanced settings. Rename the trigger with domain wording when it is clearer, like "View shortcuts". Keep the default collapsed so the summary stays scannable. Don't put primary content in the collapsible region. Don't stack several as a pseudo-accordion; use Accordion so sections are grouped. A card carries secondary detail that most readers skip, for example changelogs, advanced settings, or long descriptions under a summary. Several stacked disclosures belong together; use Accordion instead so only one section expands at a time and headings are grouped. The trigger button sets aria-expanded and points at the content region; while collapsed the region is aria-hidden and inert, and the chevron rotates as the height animates. Supports controlled (expanded) and uncontrolled (defaultExpanded) usage. The height animation uses the grid-rows technique, so any content height animates smoothly at any width without JavaScript measurement. field: A deep form seam that connects labels, descriptions, errors, and required state. Label Visible label wired to the control with htmlFor; carries the required marker when required is set. Write errors that say how to fix the value, not just that it is invalid. Keep descriptions to one sentence; move longer explanations to an Alert with appearance="callout" or a help page. Don't nest more than one control in a Field; use Fieldset for groups. Don't mark a field required visually without the required prop, or the attribute and marker drift apart. Don't clear the error while the value is still invalid; re-validate on change. A control needs a visible label, help text, or validation message. The control already owns an equivalent form-label composition. Field provides the id and ARIA relationships consumed by its child control. Keep labels readable and let long error messages wrap. The label is wired to the control with htmlFor, so clicking the label focuses the control. Description and error text are linked to Input and TextArea children through aria-describedby automatically. Setting error marks the control aria-invalid and renders the message in error color. The required indicator is decorative; the underlying control keeps the native required attribute. Custom controls can join the same wiring through the exported useFieldControl hook and mergeDescriptionIds helper. Label, description, and error Field wires the label, help text, and error message to the control inside it automatically. Choice controls Checkbox and Switch render the Field label instead of their own when nested inside one. Account profile Pair a required profile value with a clear validation message.
fieldset: A semantic fieldset/legend group for related fields, with optional help text linked to the whole group. Fieldset The native grouping element; setting disabled on it disables every control inside. Legend Names the group so screen readers announce it when focus enters any field. Description Optional help text for the whole group, linked with aria-describedby. Children The related Fields or controls, laid out in a single-column grid by default. Group controls that together answer one question, like an address block. Keep the legend short; it is repeated before every field inside. Nest Field components inside so labels and errors still work per control. Don't wrap a single control in a Fieldset; Field alone is enough. Don't use Fieldset as a visual card for unrelated content; use Card. Several controls together answer one question, such as an address block or a set of related checkboxes. A single labeled control is enough; use Field on its own instead. The legend names the group for assistive technology; the disabled attribute disables every control inside, as native fieldsets do. Children lay out in a single-column grid; add your own grid classes inside for multi-column rows. Renders a real fieldset/legend pair, so screen readers announce the legend when entering the group. The description is exposed through aria-describedby on the fieldset. Grouping fields Related Fields sit under one legend so the group is announced as a unit. Group description Help text below the legend is linked to the fieldset with aria-describedby.
file-upload: A drag-and-drop zone with a browse action and a removable file list. Drop zone The drag target that highlights on drag-over and holds the browse action. Browse action The explicit button that opens the file picker without drag-and-drop. File list Rows with the name, size, and a remove action per file. State accepted types and size limits in the description. Mirror the caller-owned value so removals stay in sync. Use accept to narrow the picker, then validate again on the server. Don't auto-upload on selection without telling the user. Don't use it for a single text reference; use Input. Don't swallow rejected files silently; surface why a file was refused. The zone fills its container and the file list wraps below. The native file input is visually hidden; the visible Browse button opens it and the label still points at the input. Column direction The same container stacks children vertically with consistent gaps and start alignment.
floating-action-button: A fixed-position primary action button for the single most important creation task on a screen. Button The round, fixed-position button named by the required label prop. Always provide label so the icon-only button has an accessible name. Use extendedLabel where space allows for extra clarity. Don't use it for destructive or secondary actions. floating-panel: A non-modal panel anchored to a viewport corner for tools that coexist with the page. Panel The non-modal surface pinned to a viewport corner; the page stays interactive behind it. Header The title row with a close button, naming the panel for assistive technology. Body The caller's companion content, like clipboard history or shortcuts. Use for companion tooling the user keeps open while working, like history or inspectors. Pick an anchor corner that doesn't cover the page's primary navigation. Tasks that demand full attention or decisions; use Dialog instead. Non-modal: the page stays interactive, focus is not trapped, and the panel closes via its close button or Escape. Fixed width capped to the viewport with margins on every side, so it never covers edge-to-edge on phones. Renders as a non-modal role="dialog" named by its title; aria-modal is not set. Because focus is not trapped, the panel participates in the natural tab order. Escape Closes the panel when focus is inside it. floating-toolbar: A floating contextual toolbar that appears near a selection or anchored element, with roving tabindex and arrow-key navigation. Toolbar Floating toolbar surface positioned by the caller near its anchor. Controls Caller-supplied buttons reached with arrow keys through a roving tabindex. Don't trap focus; it stays a single tab stop with arrow-key movement. Actions apply to a transient context such as a text selection or a hovered row and should appear right next to it. Arrow Left Arrow Up Moves focus to the previous control, wrapping at the start. Home End Moves focus to the first or last control. Custom action set Any buttons work inside; the toolbar manages focus movement across whatever controls it contains.
focus-trap: Keeps Tab and Shift+Tab focus cycling within a container and restores focus when deactivated. Trap container The div that listens for Tab and queries its own focusable descendants. The content is part of the normal page flow; trapping focus there would strand keyboard users. Use a plain container instead. Renders a plain div with no intrinsic layout, so the trapped region adapts to whatever container styles you apply. When the trap activates, focus moves to its first focusable element if focus was outside. form-error-summary: A top-of-form alert that lists validation errors as anchor links which focus the offending field. Alert container A role=alert region, so new validation failures are announced as soon as it renders. Heading A customizable title summarizing the failure count or context.
